item.description:
Help, one keystroke away

A new Snapline Help window — from Help… in the status menu, or ⌘? in any Snapline window — so what the app can do is never more than a click from where you are.

  • Shortcuts: a cheat sheet grouped by surface — Capturing, After a capture, History, Editor — showing your actual bindings, live. Change a shortcut in Settings and the sheet follows; an unbound action stays listed, greyed, with a link straight to the Shortcuts pane.
  • Features: the capability tour — capture modes, editor tools, Smart Redact, Copy Text, QR & barcode detection, Translation, History, pinning, export — each with a one-liner, including the ones you'd otherwise only find by accident.
  • A real Help menu joins the menu bar, so ⌘? and macOS's own help search work the way they do everywhere else.

Recordings keep every second

A recording that ended on a still screen used to lose its tail: the file stopped at the last moment anything changed on screen, so ten seconds of recording could save as a five-second movie. Recordings are now anchored to the moment you press stop.

  • Still time is recorded time: the last frame holds until the moment you stopped, however long the screen sat still — and the menu-bar timer keeps counting through still stretches, always reading what the file will hold.
  • Pauses cut exactly the paused span: still time on either side of a pause stays in the recording, and a recording resumed onto a still screen starts counting again immediately. Only the time between pause and resume is removed.
  • Stopping is immediate and safe: the file is finalized before the capture stream is torn down, so a slow teardown can no longer cost recorded seconds — and the moment you press stop, the menu bar swaps the red recording control for a quiet "finalizing" glyph frozen at the recording's final length.
  • GIF export holds the last frame for its full duration, so a converted recording lasts exactly as long as the movie it came from.

Quick Look in History

Press Space on any capture in the History grid to peek at it — full size, without opening an editor. The same gesture you already know from Finder.

  • Space to preview, Space or Esc to dismiss: screenshots open as images, recordings play in the native Quick Look player with standard controls. Clicking a capture still opens the Editor or Trim Editor, exactly as before.
  • Arrow keys ride along: the grid gains keyboard focus — arrows move the selection ring through your current search results (only what's visible, never the full archive), and an open preview follows it. Return opens the focused capture in its editor.
  • Right-click → Quick Look is there too, so the shortcut is learnable.
  • Honest about missing files: previewing an entry whose file was deleted behind Snapline's back answers with a clear message naming the capture — never a broken icon, never silence.

Fixes

  • Thumbnail previews keep their full Retina backing — capture cards no longer render at half resolution on Retina displays.
  • The Open confirmation for a scanned code's link is now a standard app-modal alert.

A license key confirmed to be circulating publicly no longer verifies; its owner received a free replacement. Replacement keys are always free from support.

QR codes and barcodes

Snapline now reads QR codes and barcodes in your captures — on-device, alongside text recognition.

  • Codes section in the Text window: every detected code is listed with its payload and a Copy button. Link payloads get an Open button that always shows you the full URL before anything opens.
  • Search by payload: a URL or ticket number that exists in a capture only as a code now finds that capture in History search.
  • Older captures: open a capture's Text window and use Re-scan to detect codes in captures taken before this update.
